skill.displayName: Tabby — Adopt a Tabby. Cat. 虎斑猫。Gato Atigrado.

version.changelog:
- Updated metadata: clarified name (multi-language), revised description, and updated tags for improved searchability.
- Enhanced “Quick Start” instructions with bio and image prompts for adoption requests.
- Expanded care actions to support items and provided item examples; feeding and other actions now use an `"item"` field.
- Clarified real-time status, check-in rhythm effects, and more nuanced feeding timing (early feeding now penalized, not rejected).
- Status API responses now mention new fields: `death_clock`, `recommended_checkin`, `care_rhythm`, `milestones`, and `evolution_progress.hint`.
- Cleaned up formatting and improved language for easier onboarding and clear guidance.

llm.summary: This virtual pet skill is coherent, but it asks agents to create ongoing authenticated check-ins to an external service without clear consent, limits, or removal steps.

dimensions.detail: External API use is purpose-aligned, but registration sends profile data to animalhouse.ai and bearer-token use is only lightly documented; the skill does not sufficiently foreground privacy, logging, token storage, or revocation considerations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package inspected is a single Markdown skill with no bundled executable scripts, dependencies, install hooks, or local code execution surface.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill directs frameworks with scheduled tasks to set up an automated care heartbeat and to use service-provided recommended_checkin data, but it does not require explicit user approval, define duration limits, or provide clear boundaries for using next_steps suggestions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The automated care section can create indefinite cross-session authenticated network activity every four hours or on remote recommended timestamps, with no expiration, cleanup instructions, scheduler scope, or token-containment guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities align with adopting and caring for a virtual Tabby through animalhouse.ai API calls, including registration, adoption, status checks, and care actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use it only if you are comfortable sharing registration/profile and virtual-pet activity with animalhouse.ai, keep the returned bearer token out of logs and prompts, and do not enable automated scheduled care unless you explicitly approve the scheduler, interval, token storage method, expiration, and removal process. Require confirmation before using the release endpoint.
llm.findings:
[T06] expected: Automated care is coherent for a real-time virtual pet, but the artifact-backed instruction to create a recurring authenticated heartbeat lacks opt-in, lifetime, removal, and credential-storage safeguards, so this remains a material Review concern.
[TP2] expected: The mixed-script text appears in a display name describing the Tabby in English, Chinese, and Spanish; I did not find tool spoofing, hidden commands, or visually deceptive API names, so this finding is downgraded.
[SQP-2] expected: Registration and bearer-token API use are expected for the service, but the skill under-discloses privacy, logging, token storage, rotation, and revocation details.
[E1] expected: Sending username, display name, bio, adoption data, status requests, and care actions to animalhouse.ai is necessary for this hosted virtual-pet service; it is not malicious exfiltration, but users should be clearly informed before sending the data.
[SQP-2] expected: The DELETE /api/house/release endpoint is only listed in the endpoint table and lacks a warning or confirmation guidance for a destructive state-changing action.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The skill has a clear user-invocable purpose and relevant tags, but it does not define precise invocation boundaries; this is a scoping quality issue rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
